POSITION HIGHLIGHTS:
The Department of Agricultural and Applied Economics (AAE) at the University of Arizona is seeking applicants for an Assistant Professor (tenure eligible) position to conduct research and teach courses related to water resources economics, or a closely related field. This is a 9-month, full-time appointment with opportunity for promotion in rank and tenure. This position is part of a strategic, interdisciplinary cluster hire designed to strengthen the University of Arizona's national leadership in water resource economics and related fields.

The position is 60% research, 30% teaching and 10% service with the expectation the candidate will teach two courses—undergraduate and/or graduate—each academic year. The successful candidate is expected to develop a nationally and internationally recognized research program, publish high-quality research in leading peer-reviewed journals, and actively pursue extramural funding in support of their research. As part of the candidate’s research capabilities, strong training and skills in economics, econometrics and analytical methods are expected. Research experience with water pricing, environmental market instruments, water institutions, policies, watershed protection, and/or regulatory frameworks applicable to the western U.S. is desired. Candidates should have the ability to work effectively within a broadly diverse community of students, scholars, and stakeholders.

Outstanding U of A benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance plans; life insurance and disability programs; sick leave and holidays; U of A/ASU/NAU tuition reduction for the employee and qualified family members; retirement plans; access to U of A recreation and cultural activities; and more!

The University of Arizona has been recognized for our innovative work-life programs. For more information about working at the University of Arizona and relocations services, please click here.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:
Conduct original, high-quality research and publish in leading peer-reviewed journals in agricultural, environmental, resource, and applied economics.
Actively pursue extramural funding to support a productive research program.
Provide economic intelligence that informs agricultural producers, water managers, and policymakers facing an era of growing water scarcity and resource allocation challenges. 
Work with interdisciplinary teams spanning the social sciences, natural sciences, health and food sciences, and/or engineering as part of the Irrigated Agroecosystems Science and Engineering Cluster Hire cohort.
Teach a total of two undergraduate and/or graduate courses a year.
Supervise M.S. student theses and undergraduate research projects.
Participate in faculty governance through service on departmental committees.
Provide professional and public service as appropriate.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:
Demonstrate a commitment to collaboration and engagement with various students, scholars, and stakeholders.
Strong economic training and skills.
Strong communication and mentoring skills.
Strong econometrics and analytic skills.
Commitment to collegiality and ability to work collaboratively within academic environments. 

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
Ph.D. degree in agricultural economics or economics, or a closely related discipline.
Potential ability to publish in leading Agricultural Economic, Environmental, or Economic journals.
Demonstrated capacity to provide economic intelligence for growers, water managers, and policymakers facing an era of growing water scarcity and resource allocation challenges.
Demonstrated commitment to effectively teach Agricultural and Applied Economics undergraduate and graduate students.
Demonstrated ability or commitment to working effectively in interdisciplinary teams spanning the social sciences, natural sciences, and engineering.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Demonstrated ability to publish in leading Agricultural Economic, Environmental, or Economic journals.
Demonstrated ability to working and communicating effectively within a broad community of scholars, stakeholders, and students.
Demonstrated ability to translate science into actionable guidance for agricultural businesses and communities.
Expertise in water institutions, policies, or issues applicable to the western U.S.
Expertise in water pricing, environmental market instruments, watershed protection, or regulatory frameworks.
Expertise on how water scarcity affects farm profitability and regional economic resilience.
